# Day zero

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

A fresh clone of the template to a declared, gated, pushed product, in order — then [the one path](the-one-path.md). Every command runs from the clone's root.

1. `git clone --branch <tag> <the template's repository> <product> && cd <product>` — a release tag (`v<version>`) arrives on a detached HEAD; `setup.sh` makes `main` at it
2. `./scripts/setup.sh` — the venv, this checkout's database, `.env` from `.env.example` and the identity seed
3. `uv run python manage.py declare <ns>` — declares the clone a product: `quality/local/rules.yaml` gets `rule_id_namespace: <ns>` and `template_rule_ids_through: <n>` (the highest integer rule id the template has minted, computed from the tree), `scripts/local/template-base` the template commit the clone stands on (`git merge-base HEAD v<version>` once a `template` remote exists, else `HEAD`). `<ns>` is one lowercase word (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, never `djb`); your rules are `<ns>-<n>`, your valves `# rule-<ns>-<n>:`. A second run changes nothing unless a release moved them
4. `git add quality/local/rules.yaml scripts/local/template-base && git commit -m "<ns>: the product declares itself"` — through the hook, which runs `--fast` on every commit. A script the product adds under `scripts/local/` gets its row in `docs/product/instruments.local.md` before the commit, or the hook's instrument census refuses it: `uncensused: <path> — a drawer instrument's row is in instruments.local.md` (`scripts/goalpost_scan.py:862`)
5. `DJB_GATE_SANCTION="first-run: <who> green on the empty product" ./scripts/check.sh > "$PWD/gate-first-run.log" 2>&1` — the one full gate a product types by hand; never piped (a pipe is exit 2). On a product it runs every leg but the platform's own tests — `gate-tests`, `pytest-x2`'s partition proof and the `selftest` unit's engine selftest (`house-rules-engine`) each print that they are not a product's to pay for; `gate-tests` still runs your `quality/local/tests`, the engine still self-tests your drawer's own rules, `drive_preamble` (the tripwire every drive stands on) runs as on the template, and `pytest-x2` runs the product's own apps once — the first run is the long one, and the gate prints its own wall on its last line, `ok: all checks passed (<n>s)`. Exit 0 clean · 1 violations · 2 enforcement broken. From here the per-change gate is the one path's `--loop --here "<app>: <why>"` (`quality/djb/modes.py:412`)
6. `git remote rename origin template && git remote add origin <your product's repository>` — a tag clone's `origin` is the template; `template` is the remote `take_release.sh` fetches releases from (`--remote <name>` names another), and `origin` becomes yours
7. `git push -u origin main` — the first push seeds main: the remote has no main, so the pre-push hook lets it through (`pre-push: main seeded`) and still demands a green full gate of the tree (it honours a banked one, or runs the gate itself) — the gate measures the working tree, untracked and not-ignored files included, so commit your own notes and ledgers as you write them or ignore them. Every later move of main is a pull request: `./scripts/pm_push.sh --pr` from a `pm/*` branch. A new `pm/*` branch is a new derived database, so a `./scripts/serve.sh` or `./scripts/worker.sh` still running from the last branch serves that branch's database: restart both on the new branch (`./scripts/kill_mine.sh --kill`, then start them again) (`scripts/db.sh:154`)
8. `gh repo edit <owner>/<repo> --enable-auto-merge && gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets --input deploy/ruleset.json` — the owner's one-time lines, in order, before the first `--pr`: auto-merge on, then the ruleset that requires the CI checks `verdict` and `gate-verdict` on main. Without the ruleset `gh pr merge --auto` merges at once, so `--pr` refuses, leaving its pull request open and unmerged, and prints these two lines with your repository filled in (`quality/djb/rituals/push.py:560`)
9. `docs/product/north-star.md` — who you serve and what shipped means — your first pull request. The next `--pr` waits for this one to merge: the ruleset's checks are strict, so a pull request opened while another is open turns BEHIND when that one merges, and its run cannot merge it until origin/main is merged into the branch

**Your first app.** After `newapp`, run `uv run python manage.py declare <ns>` again: it adds `DJB_IDENTITY_SHAPE=platform_apps=own` to `.env` and `identity_shape: platform_apps=own` to `quality/local/rules.yaml` (the template's census of its own app set then skips your app; `apps/core/management/commands/declare.py:207`). Commit the drawer: it carries the declaration, so your CI needs nothing set.

**Rename nothing** means the paths and names in the tree — files, apps, commands. Your repository's name and its git remotes are yours (step 6).

**The CPU.** Every image the dev stack pulls is a multi-architecture index (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`) except MinIO, which is one `linux/arm64` manifest on the template owner's ECR Public mirror because no registry still serves that release's amd64 layers — so an Apple-silicon or other arm64 host runs it natively, and an amd64 laptop runs it under Docker's arm64 emulation (Docker Desktop ships it; a Linux host needs QEMU's binfmt handlers installed), slower and otherwise the same. (`compose.yaml:414`)

**The compose project name.** Every clone's stack is the compose project `djangobootstrap`, the name `docker ps` shows: ADR platform-1 keeps it as the one deliberate exception to `PRODUCT_NAME`, because it is infrastructure identity — the containers and volumes key on it, and renaming it orphans a running stack and its data. (`compose.yaml:30`)

## A local admin and a tenant

- `uv run python manage.py seed` — a laptop's tenant `acme`, `owner@example.com`, `member@example.com` and an API token printed once; DEBUG only, and a second run is another token
- `uv run python manage.py issue_token --email <email> --tenant <slug> --name <label> --scope '*'` — a token for the machine door (REST, MCP), printed once; narrow `--scope` to the job
- `uv run python manage.py zitadel_first_admin --email <you>` — a deployment's first human: the link where they set their own password; refused once a tenant exists
- `uv run python manage.py bootstrap_tenant --email <you>` — after that first sign-in: the installation's first tenant, with you its owner
- `uv run python manage.py grant_staff --email <email> --as <a superuser's email>` — staff (opens `/admin/`), audited; the road that replaces `createsuperuser`

## What you write

- `apps/<your app>/` — your apps — `newapp` makes one; `apps/core/roles.py` is yours too
- `frontend/` — your screens, past the worked example's
- `quality/local/` — your drawer: the declaration, your rules `<ns>-<n>` and their fixtures
- `scripts/local/` — `template-base`, which `declare` writes and `./scripts/take_release.sh <tag>` rewrites to the tag it took; run `declare <ns>` again after a take to move the rule ceiling and, since 2.5.0a9, to carry `identity_shape:` into the drawer — commit it
- `docs/product/north-star.md` — who you serve and what shipped means
- `docs/product/operating-protocol.md` — the autonomy dial and the readout cadence
- `docs/product/architecture.md` — your own copy: one `divergence: <path> — <reason>` line per platform file you edit
- `README.md` — your product's front page
- the other ledgers, skeletons on day zero, which the product manager fills (open a session and say *"you're the PM"*): `docs/product/design-agreements.md`, `docs/product/goal-posts.md`, `docs/product/in-flight.md`, `docs/product/misses.md`, `docs/product/pilot-readiness.md`, `docs/product/queue-detail.md`, `docs/product/queue.md`, `docs/product/readouts.md`, `docs/product/rep-day.md`, `docs/product/threat-model.md`

Everything else is the platform's: it arrives by `./scripts/take_release.sh <tag>`, and the hook refuses a commit to it.
